versionConflict.title: Version Conflicts
versionConflict.description: These games have version data to sort out: library entries that share one product id, or scanned folders that could not be placed automatically. Pick a game to edit all of its versions.
versionConflict.mergeWarning: On save these duplicate entries are deleted; their directories stay as versions of this game:

versions.empty: This game has no versions left to edit
versions.missingWarning: {{folders}} directory(ies) are missing — those versions cannot be launched
versions.duplicateWarning: Several versions point at the same directory — separate them first
versions.ignoreDropped: Add ignored folders to the scanner exclude list so scans stop reporting them

conflictCenter.title: Conflicts
conflictCenter.description: Everything a scan can leave for you to decide lands here: the version data of your library (entries sharing a product id, folders that could not be placed) and the tag names that collided while ingesting. Pick a game to edit all of its versions.

tagConflict.pendingHint: Ingestion no longer merges by text, so two entries sharing a name are listed here for you to decide whether they mean the same thing.
tagConflict.ignoredHint: These were left as they are — the same spelling will not ask again. Accepting either side brings the decision back.
tagConflict.moveVsMerge: "Merge…" means the two entries are really the same concept (or this one should not exist) — pick a target and fold them into one; when both sides have a name in the same language you confirm per language which to keep. "Fix index" means this source points at the wrong entry — only the index moves, both entries stay.

verdict.same: Identical spelling → likely the same concept
verdict.alias: Matches the other side's alias / another language's spelling → likely the same concept
verdict.similar: English names are near-identical → likely the same concept
verdict.different: Spellings do not line up → possibly a different concept

compare.noComparableHint: Apart from the conflicting language these two share no language, so there is nothing to compare. Scraping another locale of that source fills it in.
